chapters.1.summary: King David is old and weak. His son Adonijah declares himself king with the support of Joab and the priest Abiathar. He holds a feast and leaves out Solomon and the prophet Nathan. Nathan sends Bathsheba to remind David of his oath about Solomon. Nathan follows her in and confirms her report. David orders Solomon to ride the royal mule to Gihon. Zadok the priest anoints him, and the city shouts. Adonijah’s guests scatter, and he begs Solomon for his life.
chapters.1.lds: Who speaks for Solomon when David must choose the next king?
chapters.2.summary: David tells Solomon to keep the LORD’s law and to deal with Joab and Shimei. David dies after forty years as king. Adonijah asks Bathsheba to request David’s last attendant, Abishag, as his wife. Solomon reads this as a claim to the throne and has him killed. He sends the priest Abiathar home to Anathoth. Joab flees to the altar and is killed there. Shimei is confined to Jerusalem and dies when he leaves it. The kingdom is now firmly in Solomon’s hand.
chapters.2.lds: How does Solomon explain his orders against each rival?
chapters.3.summary: Solomon marries Pharaoh’s daughter and brings her to Jerusalem. He offers sacrifices at Gibeon, and the LORD appears to him in a dream. God tells him to ask for what he wants. Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people. God is pleased and adds riches and honor. Two prostitutes then come to him, each claiming the same living baby. Solomon calls for a sword to divide the child. The true mother gives up her claim, and he returns the child to her.
chapters.3.lds: Come, Follow Me encourages seeking discernment between right and wrong. What does Solomon ask for in verse 9, and for whose benefit?
chapters.4.summary: The chapter lists Solomon’s chief officials. Twelve officers govern twelve districts. Each district supplies the king’s household for one month of the year. Judah and Israel are as many as the sand, eating and drinking. The court uses huge amounts of flour, meal, and meat each day. Everyone lives safely under his own vine and fig tree. God gives Solomon wisdom beyond all the people of the East. He speaks three thousand proverbs and teaches about trees and animals.
chapters.4.lds: Who provides the food that supports Solomon’s court?
chapters.5.summary: King Hiram of Tyre sends greetings to Solomon. Solomon says he will build a house for the LORD’s name. He asks for cedar from Lebanon, cut by skilled Sidonians. Hiram agrees and floats the logs down the coast. Solomon pays him each year in wheat and oil. The two kings make a treaty. Solomon drafts thirty thousand Israelites to work in Lebanon in shifts. Thousands more carry loads and cut great stones for the foundation.
chapters.5.lds: What does temple building require from the workers and their families?
chapters.6.summary: Solomon begins the temple in the fourth year of his reign. The house is sixty cubits long, twenty wide, and thirty high. Its stones are finished at the quarry, so no iron tool is heard on site. The LORD tells Solomon the promise holds if he keeps the commandments. The inside is lined with cedar and covered with gold. Two gold-covered cherubim stand in the inner room. The walls and doors are carved with palms and flowers. The work takes seven years.
chapters.6.lds: Come, Follow Me invites reflection on sacred space and temple symbols. What condition does verse 12 attach to the building?
chapters.7.summary: Solomon spends thirteen years building his own palace. It includes the House of the Forest of Lebanon and a hall for judging. He builds a similar house for Pharaoh’s daughter. He brings Hiram, a bronze worker, from Tyre. Hiram casts two great pillars named Jachin and Boaz. He makes a huge basin called the sea, set on twelve bronze oxen. He makes ten wheeled stands, basins, pots, and shovels. Solomon adds the gold furnishings and David’s dedicated treasures.
chapters.7.lds: The older Church manual compares the bronze sea with baptism. What does verse 14 say about the craftsman’s family and skill?
chapters.8.summary: The elders and priests bring the ark into the temple. A cloud fills the house, and the priests cannot stand to serve. Solomon blesses the people and prays before the altar. He says heaven itself cannot contain God, much less this house. He asks God to hear prayers made toward it. He names drought, famine, defeat, and exile as times to pray. He asks God to hear the foreigner too. Israel then offers sacrifices and keeps a feast for fourteen days.
chapters.8.lds: Come, Follow Me connects the dedication prayer with temple covenants and walking in God’s ways. Whom does Solomon pray for in verses 41–43?
chapters.9.summary: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time and accepts the temple. If Solomon walks as David did, his throne will last. If Israel turns to other gods, the land and the house will be lost. Solomon gives Hiram twenty towns in Galilee, and Hiram is not pleased. Solomon uses forced labor to build Jerusalem’s wall, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer. The remaining Canaanite peoples are made laborers. Israelites serve as soldiers and officers. Solomon builds ships on the Red Sea that bring gold from Ophir.
chapters.9.lds: Come, Follow Me studies God’s promises and the responsibility to keep covenants. What does verse 7 say could happen to the temple?
chapters.10.summary: The queen of Sheba hears of Solomon and comes to test him with hard questions. He answers them all. She sees his house, his table, his servants, and his offerings. She says the report she heard was not even half the truth. She blesses the LORD, who made him king to do justice. They exchange rich gifts, and she goes home. Solomon’s yearly gold, his ivory throne, and his golden cups are described. He gathers chariots and buys horses from Egypt.
chapters.10.lds: What impresses the queen besides Solomon’s wealth?
chapters.11.summary: Solomon loves many foreign women and has a thousand wives and concubines. In his old age they turn his heart to other gods. He builds high places for the gods of Moab and Ammon. The LORD says the kingdom will be torn from his son. One tribe will remain for David’s sake. Enemies rise in Edom and Damascus. The prophet Ahijah tears a new cloak and gives ten pieces to an officer, Jeroboam. Solomon tries to kill Jeroboam, who flees to Egypt until Solomon dies.
chapters.11.lds: Come, Follow Me asks readers to examine influences that turn their hearts from God. What does Ahijah do with the garment in verse 30?
chapters.12.summary: Rehoboam goes to Shechem to be made king. Jeroboam and the people ask him to lighten Solomon’s heavy labor. The old advisers tell him to serve the people and speak kindly. The young men tell him to promise a heavier yoke. He follows the young men and threatens scorpions for whips. Ten tribes reject David’s house and make Jeroboam king. A prophet stops Rehoboam from going to war. Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan to keep his people from Jerusalem.
chapters.12.lds: Come, Follow Me studies the effect of leaders’ choices and the need for good counsel. What do the people offer Rehoboam in verse 4?
chapters.13.summary: A man of God from Judah cries out against Jeroboam’s altar at Bethel. The altar splits, and the king’s hand withers and is healed. The man refuses the king’s meal, as God commanded him. An old prophet of Bethel rides after him. The old man lies and says an angel told him to bring the visitor home. The man of God eats, and a word comes that he will die. A lion kills him on the road and stands beside the body. The old prophet buries him in his own tomb.
chapters.13.lds: Why does the visiting prophet accept a claim that changes his earlier command?
chapters.14.summary: Jeroboam’s son falls sick. He sends his wife in disguise to the prophet Ahijah at Shiloh. Ahijah is blind, but the LORD tells him who is coming. He says Jeroboam’s whole house will be cut off for its idols. The child will die when she reaches home. Israel itself will be uprooted and scattered. In Judah, Rehoboam’s people build high places and sacred pillars. Shishak king of Egypt takes the temple’s treasures and Solomon’s gold shields.
chapters.14.lds: How does Ahijah’s message affect Jeroboam’s wife and child?
chapters.15.summary: Abijam rules Judah three years and follows his father’s sins. For David’s sake the LORD keeps a lamp in Jerusalem. Asa rules forty-one years and does what is right. He removes idols and even deposes his grandmother for her idol. Baasha of Israel fortifies Ramah to block Judah. Asa sends temple and palace treasure to Ben Hadad of Syria. Ben Hadad attacks northern Israel, and Baasha withdraws. In Israel, Baasha has killed Nadab and all Jeroboam’s house.
chapters.15.lds: What does Asa give away to gain help against Baasha?
chapters.16.summary: A prophet tells Baasha that his house will end like Jeroboam’s. His son Elah is killed while drunk by Zimri, a chariot commander. Zimri rules seven days and burns the palace over himself. Omri defeats a rival and becomes king. He buys the hill of Samaria and builds his capital there. His son Ahab marries Jezebel of Sidon and builds a temple for Baal. Ahab does more evil than all before him. In his days a man rebuilds Jericho at the cost of two sons.
chapters.16.lds: How do the changes of kings affect their families and towns?
chapters.17.summary: Elijah tells Ahab there will be no dew or rain except at his word. The LORD hides him by a brook, where ravens bring him food. The brook dries up. The LORD sends him to a widow in Zarephath, a town of Sidon. She is gathering sticks to cook a last meal for herself and her son. Elijah asks for a small cake first and promises the flour and oil will last. They do. Later her son dies, Elijah prays, and the boy lives again.
chapters.17.lds: Come, Follow Me studies the widow’s trust amid scarcity. What does the widow have left in verse 12?
chapters.18.summary: In the third year of drought the LORD sends Elijah to Ahab. Ahab’s steward Obadiah has hidden a hundred prophets from Jezebel. Elijah gathers Israel and four hundred fifty prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. Each side prepares a bull, and the God who answers by fire is God. Baal’s prophets cry out all day, and nothing happens. Elijah rebuilds the LORD’s altar and drenches it with water. He prays, and fire falls and burns up everything. The people confess the LORD, Baal’s prophets are killed, and rain comes.
chapters.18.lds: Come, Follow Me uses Elijah’s challenge to examine commitment to God. How do the people answer Elijah’s question in verse 21?
chapters.19.summary: Jezebel swears to kill Elijah, and he runs for his life. In the wilderness he sits under a tree and asks to die. An angel twice wakes him and gives him food and water. He travels forty days to Horeb, the mountain of God. There a wind, an earthquake, and a fire pass, and then a quiet voice. Elijah says he alone is left. The LORD sends him to anoint two kings and Elisha. Elisha leaves his oxen and follows him.
chapters.19.lds: Come, Follow Me studies the quiet voice and Elisha’s willingness to respond. How many does the LORD say remain faithful in verse 18?
chapters.20.summary: Ben Hadad of Syria besieges Samaria and demands Ahab’s treasure and family. A prophet promises Ahab victory, and Israel wins. The Syrians decide the LORD is a god of the hills only. They return in spring and lose again on the plain. Ben Hadad’s servants come in sackcloth to beg for his life. Ahab calls him “my brother” and makes a treaty. A prophet in disguise tells Ahab a story and condemns him with it. Ahab goes home sullen and angry.
chapters.20.lds: Why does the prophet challenge Ahab after his victory?
chapters.21.summary: Naboth owns a vineyard beside Ahab’s palace in Jezreel. Ahab offers him money or a better vineyard, and Naboth refuses. Ahab lies on his bed and will not eat. Jezebel writes letters in his name to the town’s elders. Two false witnesses accuse Naboth of cursing God and the king. He is stoned, and Ahab goes down to take the vineyard. Elijah meets him there with the LORD’s sentence on his house. Ahab humbles himself, and the disaster is delayed to his son’s time.
chapters.21.lds: How do Ahab and Jezebel use their power against Naboth? What does Elijah say about their actions?
chapters.22.summary: Jehoshaphat of Judah visits Ahab, who wants to retake Ramoth Gilead. Four hundred prophets promise success. Jehoshaphat asks for one more, and Ahab names Micaiah, whom he hates. Micaiah sees Israel scattered like sheep without a shepherd. He describes a lying spirit sent into the mouths of Ahab’s prophets. Ahab jails him and goes to battle in disguise. A random arrow strikes Ahab between the plates of his armor. He dies at evening, and dogs lick his blood in Samaria.
chapters.22.lds: The older Church manual reads the lying spirit as God allowing deception. What does the messenger ask Micaiah to do in verse 13?
